title: Storage Collected in Advance in a Kestrel Pre-Owned Retail Redemption Figure
content:
For storage a redemption figure collects in advance, and only for such storage, the storage is worked out as follows. Storage still to accrue on the storage lot while the figure is good is added for the days after the quote date, priced at the daily amount of the most recent storage charge — its amount divided by its billable days, the first one listed where two share a date — or at the daily storage fee for the tier where that charge covers no billable day or no storage charge is on record.

The vehicle is on the storage lot when the most recent condition report (the first one listed where two share a date) is dated on or after the repossession date. Periods are counted in calendar days from the repossession date (not counted).

| Vehicle and period running on the quote date | Days projected after the quote date |
|---|---|
| On the storage lot, while a recorded state reinstatement period longer than the company window is running | through the last day of the state period |
| On the storage lot, while the company reinstatement window is running and no longer state period is recorded | through the last day of the company window |
| Otherwise, including no condition report dated on or after the repossession date | no storage is projected |

| Tier | Company reinstatement window (calendar days) |
|---|---|
| Kestrel Pre-Owned Retail Tier 5, Tier 4, Tier 3 | 10 |
| Kestrel Pre-Owned Retail Tier 2, Tier 1 | 15 |
| Kestrel Pre-Owned Retail Tier 1+ | 21 |

**Hypothetical case.** Repossession on day 0, lot intake on day 2, state period 30 days, quote on day 12, most recent storage charge $180.00 for 9 billable days (a daily amount of $20.00): 18 days are projected, $360.00. With a quote on day 30, nothing is projected — no day of the period remains after the quote date.

### Storage billed when the vehicle leaves the lot

Storage is billed only for days the vehicle is on the storage lot, and each such day only once. The lot days of an involuntary recovery whose most recent condition report is dated after the repossession date run from the day after that lot-intake date, the nights before it being the agency's holding, billed on its transport charge and never as storage; the lot days of a voluntary surrender run from the repossession date itself; any other lot days run from the day after the repossession date. A lot day up to and including the latest statement date on which a storage charge was billed is billed by that charge, whatever the charge came to, and a lot day collected in a redemption figure or a reinstatement amount or counted into a deficiency quote is not billed again. Every other lot day through the release or sale date is charged at the daily storage fee once the free days are used up, and it is billed when the vehicle leaves the lot. The free days for that charge — the charge billed when the vehicle leaves the lot — follow the recovery history: an involuntary recovery of a contract that shows an earlier reinstatement payment has none, a voluntary surrender of a contract that shows no reinstatement payment has the surrender free days of 7, and any other recovery has the free days for the tier, in each case less any free days an earlier storage charge for the same repossession already set against its stored days.
